The drow abandons the appearance of a permanent kingdom once it has served its purpose, and Athrogate remains with him. Entreri's relationship with Calihye ends in violence when the grief and divided loyalties left by Ellery's death overwhelm their fragile trust. Entreri believes Calihye dead; Jarlaxle secretly has her restored and arranges for Kimmuriel to remove the memories tying her to Entreri, leaving her alive but outside his life. Jarlaxle then leads Entreri to the place of his childhood and forces the history he has buried into the open. Entreri confronts the men and institutions responsible for abuse, abandonment and his entry into a life of killing. He takes vengeance on those still within reach but rejects the idea that blood, a father or an abuser has the right to define what he becomes. He survives the journey with his partnership with Jarlaxle damaged yet intact, carrying self-knowledge rather than the final emptiness he once sought through defeating Drizzt.
recaps.in_short: Jarlaxle and Artemis Entreri return from Zhengyi's ruin owing explanations to Gareth Dragonsbane and the dragon sisters, while Entreri struggles with shadow magic and a fragile relationship with Calihye. Jarlaxle answers the pressure with a larger deception: he establishes Castle D'aerthe in Vaasa and presents himself as a would-be ruler, luring the Citadel of Assassins into exposing its strength. With Athrogate, Kimmuriel and Bregan D'aerthe, he maneuvers Gareth's champions and the assassins into a confrontation that breaks the Citadel without leaving him king. Entreri and Calihye turn on one another, and he believes he kills her; Jarlaxle secretly saves her and has her memories of Entreri removed. Jarlaxle then takes Entreri back toward his childhood home. Forced to confront the abuse, betrayal and abandonment behind his chosen identity, Entreri kills those he holds responsible but refuses to let ancestry dictate his future. He and Jarlaxle remain uneasy partners, and Entreri ends the trilogy changed by attachments he can no longer dismiss as weakness.

recaps.text: Previously: Jarlaxle and Artemis Entreri left Calimport after apparently destroying Crenshinibon, the Crystal Shard whose history had repeatedly intersected Entreri's rivalry with Drizzt Do'Urden. In the Bloodstone Lands they joined an expedition into a Vaasan ruin sustained by the dead Witch-King Zhengyi's magic. The company rescued the half-orc Arrayan but lost several members, and Commander Ellery and the wizard Canthan were exposed as conspirators and killed. The dwarf Athrogate broke with them and became Jarlaxle's ally. Entreri formed an uneasy bond with Calihye. In the final struggle, his vampiric dagger drained a creature of living shadow, leaving him physically renewed, altered in appearance and connected to shadow magic. Jarlaxle emerged with relics and obligations to local powers, including the dragon sisters Ilnezhara and Tazmikella, while Gareth Dragonsbane's government was left to judge what the adventurers had done in Vaasa.

Jarlaxle, Entreri, Calihye and Athrogate return from the Vaasan expedition to a region full of people who want answers. King Gareth Dragonsbane must account for Ellery's death, the disturbance of Zhengyi's relics and the possibility that Jarlaxle removed dangerous magic for private use. Ilnezhara and Tazmikella are equally interested in what was recovered and regard Jarlaxle's evasions as a breach of obligations made before the mission. Entreri is no longer the man who entered the ruin. Shadow clings to him, his body has been unnaturally renewed, and Calihye's presence keeps drawing emotions he once suppressed. Jarlaxle tries to balance royal scrutiny, draconic demands and Entreri's growing distrust without surrendering either treasure or freedom. The road toward Bloodstone therefore becomes a negotiation conducted under the threat of several kinds of overwhelming force.

Gareth's champions, including the monk Kane and the intelligence master Celedon Kierney, refuse to accept the simple version of Jarlaxle's story. The dragon sisters also close off easy escape, forcing the drow to offer something more valuable than punishment: a way to expose the surviving organization behind recent violence in Vaasa. Jarlaxle presents his continued presence in the country as bait for enemies of the Bloodstone throne. Entreri sees that each promise buys time rather than trust, but he participates because the alternatives are imprisonment, a direct fight with dragons or abandoning Calihye and Athrogate. His shadow abilities help the group pass obstacles that once would have required Jarlaxle's magic, increasing both his independence and his unease about what he absorbed. By the time they leave the immediate gauntlet, Jarlaxle has turned their reckoning into permission for another dangerous operation.

Bregan D'aerthe establishes a surface fortress, Castle D'aerthe, and Jarlaxle allows rumors to portray him as a new claimant to Vaasa. Kimmuriel supplies drow troops, psionic coordination and concealment, while Athrogate gives the enterprise a visible champion. The fortress is less a capital than a lure. Knellict and the Citadel of Assassins cannot ignore an outsider occupying territory and gathering magic once associated with Zhengyi, and Gareth cannot ignore either faction if they appear ready to build a new tyranny. Jarlaxle expects both sides to move against the threat he has staged. Entreri works within the deception but grows more suspicious of the personal plans his partner keeps separate from the political one. Calihye wants him to acknowledge their bond; he answers uncertainty with control, making every disagreement resemble betrayal before either has actually chosen it.

Knellict overreaches in response to Castle D'aerthe, bringing the Citadel's agents and ambitions into the open. Jarlaxle releases enough information for Gareth's forces to strike the organization while preserving routes for Bregan D'aerthe to withdraw. The apparent contest for the title of Vaasa's king ends as a trap rather than a coronation: Jarlaxle gains room to leave, the Citadel loses its concealed advantage and Gareth avoids replacing one Witch-King with another. The personal alliance does not survive as neatly. Calihye's grief over the last expedition and Entreri's inability to trust affection turn their relationship into a confrontation. Old loyalties connected to Ellery's death surface, and Calihye attacks the man she also cares for. Entreri responds with the lethal instincts that have always protected him. He believes he has killed her, and Jarlaxle allows that belief to stand while arranging matters outside his sight.

With the Vaasan operation closing, Jarlaxle turns from kingdoms to the history Entreri refuses to discuss. He has gathered fragments about the assassin's childhood and decides that leaving the old wounds untouched will only let them continue governing every attachment Entreri forms. Entreri reads the investigation as a profound violation, especially after Calihye's apparent death, but cannot ignore information about the family and community from which he fled. Their road carries them toward the southern places where the boy who became Artemis Entreri first learned to treat feeling as a weapon others could use. Memories return unevenly: abandonment, exploitation and abuse are mixed with later explanations that Entreri no longer trusts. Jarlaxle does not offer forgiveness on anyone's behalf. He instead makes it possible for Entreri to meet the surviving people connected to those memories and choose what their blood relationship means.

Entreri confronts the people and institutions responsible for the misery of his childhood and the path that delivered him into Calimport's criminal world. He takes vengeance where he finds the guilty still within reach, but the encounters do not reveal a noble patriarch whose blood can supply a better identity. The lesson is instead that parentage, violation and abandonment explain parts of him without owning his future. Jarlaxle's interference infuriates Entreri, yet it also breaks the silence on which those memories depended. Unknown to him, Jarlaxle has kept Calihye from dying and asked Kimmuriel to remove her memories of Entreri, leaving her alive without the bond that brought them both to violence. Athrogate remains with Jarlaxle after the false kingdom in Vaasa is dismantled. Entreri and Jarlaxle survive their road together with trust badly strained but with their partnership intact. Entreri no longer defines himself solely through Drizzt, Calihye, or the men who shaped his childhood; that independence is less empty, and therefore more difficult, than the perfection he once pursued.

characters.description: A biologist nearing completion of his PhD when Earth is integrated into the System. Trapped without weapons in the Forest of the Strong, he relies on field knowledge, observation, and a willingness to adapt while searching for a way out.
characters.name: Jack Rust

characters.description: The level-9 boss directing the goblin settlement. Hobgoblins defer to this leader, whose visible abilities include fire magic.
characters.name: the Goblin Shaman

characters.description: The level-25 leader of the dungeon's ape group. He guards the group's strength-enhancing resource and agrees to face Jack in a formal boxing contest.
characters.name: the ape-group alpha

characters.description: The level-30 leader of the dungeon's earth bears. Jack shadows this powerful boss and prepares a surprise attack before the Black Wolf can claim it as prey.
characters.name: the rock bear

characters.description: The ape-group alpha whom Jack defeated and spared. Jack gives him the name Harambe as their former rivalry becomes an alliance.
characters.name: Harambe

characters.description: Harambe's young son, entrusted to Jack so he can leave the forest and find opportunities in the wider world. He is a bro-rilla who resembles the smaller gym monkeys.
characters.name: Brock

characters.description: Jack's foster mother, a retired cybersecurity professor living in Volville. She is alive after integration but appears to be watched and constrained by the faction controlling the town.
characters.name: Professor Margaret Rust

characters.description: A Henry's Fang enforcer ordered to remain with Margaret and restrict her movements. Jack forces him out of her home after discovering the arrangement.
characters.name: Hugo

characters.description: The leader of Henry's Fang, the armed faction ruling Volville through intimidation and unequal control of equipment. He is a swordsman with a history of running protection schemes.
characters.name: Henry White

characters.description: An E-grade djinn merchant affiliated with the Merchant Union. He explains the market for System goods and information, gives Jack access to credit, and applies strict commercial rules to every transaction.
characters.name: Ar'Tazul

characters.description: An unaffiliated fire wizard whose parents were killed by Henry's Fang. He is the only Volville resident to volunteer immediately when Jack asks for help against the faction.
characters.name: Edgar

characters.description: One of five Scions and the superior or patron named by Henry White. His connection to Henry's Fang places the conflict in Volville within a larger struggle involving the coming tournament.
characters.name: Gan Salin

characters.description: The leader of Flame River, one of the few major Earth factions known to have conquered an F-grade dungeon. She is identified as a leading African cultivator before the tournament.
characters.name: Vivi Aragon

characters.description: The leader of Ice Peak, a major faction based in northeastern Europe. He is identified before the tournament as one of Earth's established faction leaders.
characters.name: Alexander Petrovic

characters.description: Jack's disguised tournament identity, registered with a flip-flop as his weapon and a fabricated Dao. The persona conceals his real appearance, faction, title, and fighting path from the Scions.
characters.name: John Brown

characters.description: A C-grade Leonin who represents the Animal Kingdom as Earth's planetary overseer. She opens the integration tournament and announces its rules, rewards, and elimination structure.
characters.name: Galicia Lonahor

characters.description: A level-38 dagger fighter following the Dao of Speed. He wins his opening match before his opponent can draw a weapon, then approaches Jack with an easy familiarity.
characters.name: Dorman Whistles

characters.description: A Flame River fire cultivator who yields an early match against an Ice Peak opponent after receiving direction from his faction leader.
characters.name: Sadaka

characters.description: A level-49 Leonin Scion, Planetary Frontrunner 1, and the tournament favorite. His first match ends with his opponent dead from a single attack, prompting Jack to demand enforcement of the rules.
characters.name: Rufus Emberheart

characters.description: A homeless-looking level-38 man who approaches Jack under the title of Sage after the tournament's opening round. His purpose and capabilities are not yet clear.
characters.name: the Sage

characters.description: An older tournament fighter who follows the Dao of Martial Arts. His precise unarmed technique lets him control an armed opponent and stop a sword between three fingers.
characters.name: Li Shang

characters.description: A Shen Group competitor at level 27. Her Dao of Beauty influences the soul, but Jack withstands it and wins their tournament match.
characters.name: Chen Zexi

characters.description: An automated sparring machine in Jack's tournament residence. Enchanted through the Dao of Automation, it can train at several power levels and limits its activity to instruction and practice combat.
characters.name: the training robot

characters.description: The level-49 elite boss of the Forest of the Strong. This territorial apex predator is far stronger than Jack when he first encounters it.
characters.name: the Black Wolf

characters.description: A second, uninjured level-49 Black Wolf that appears after Jack and the primates defeat the wolf they believed was the dungeon boss.
characters.name: the second Black Wolf

characters.description: Ar'Tazul's djinn cousin, a merchant guide hired to lead Jack and Edgar through Integration City.
characters.name: Ar'Tazul's cousin

characters.description: An unnamed level-45 sharkin Scion who appears beside Gan Salin and watches Vivi Aragon with hostile interest.
characters.name: the sharkin Scion

characters.description: A D-grade projection from Exploding Sun who chooses Jack as a disciple because Jack's Dao is linked to the faction's ancestor.
characters.name: Jack's Exploding Sun mentor

characters.description: An eagle Scion competing in the integration tournament. This fighter is paired with the elephant-like Scion within the broader Scion group.
characters.name: the eagle Scion

characters.description: An elephant-like Scion competing in the integration tournament. This fighter is paired with the eagle Scion within the broader Scion group.
characters.name: the elephant-like Scion

characters.description: An unaffiliated tournament fighter known for music and an affinity with the Dao of Metal. He remains outside both major human alliances alongside Li Shang.
characters.name: the metal-Dao musician

characters.description: The metal-Dao musician, now identified by name. He and Li Shang remain neutral while Flame River and the Scions gather allies.
characters.name: Kane Vander Decken

recaps.ending: Jack wins the tournament when Rufus misses the final, but Exploding Sun withdraws its promised protection under Animal Kingdom pressure. Galicia separately cancels Jack's promised Animal Kingdom apprenticeship and permits the Scions to attack. Jack assigns his D-grade robot prize to protect the Bare Fist Brotherhood. In the ensuing battle, Sadaka and Li Shang are killed, Edgar defeats Gan Salin and collapses, and Alexander severely wounds Vivi before escaping. Rufus returns after reaching E-grade. Jack develops Iron Fist Style and kills him despite the overseer's attempted intervention. Gan Salin then attacks the exhausted Jack, but Brock and his dog pack drive him away. Brock carries Jack to the teleporter, and they depart for an unknown galactic destination. Margaret, Harambe's primates, the robot, and the surviving allies remain responsible for the Brotherhood on Earth. Gan Salin and the overseer remain hostile. Jack owes the Black Hole Church a favor and intends to become strong enough to return and take Earth from the Animal Kingdom.
recaps.in_short: Earth's integration traps biologist Jack Rust in a dungeon, where he advances through combat, befriends Harambe's primates, kills two Black Wolf bosses, and founds the Bare Fist Brotherhood. After freeing Volville from Henry's Fang, he enters the integration tournament in disguise and builds alliances with Edgar, Vivi Aragon, Dorman Whistles, Li Shang, and the Sage against the Animal Kingdom's Scions. Jack reaches E-grade with a perfect Dao Seed of the Fist and wins when Rufus Emberheart misses the final, but Exploding Sun withdraws its promised protection under Animal Kingdom pressure, and Galicia authorizes an attack. Sadaka and Li Shang die, while Vivi and Edgar are left gravely hurt or unconscious. Rufus returns at E-grade, and Jack kills him after creating Iron Fist Style. Brock saves the exhausted Jack from Gan Salin and takes him through a teleporter to an unknown destination. Jack leaves the Brotherhood defended on Earth and plans to return strong enough to challenge Animal Kingdom rule.

recaps.text: Earth is absorbed into a System that introduces levels, monsters, dungeons, and an approaching integration tournament. Jack Rust, a biologist nearing his PhD, is caught inside the Forest of the Strong, a sealed dungeon he can leave only by defeating its boss. He kills goblins with his bare hands, gains levels and Fistfighting knowledge, and uses a hidden Ice Pond to heal and strengthen himself. Scouting reveals three monster groups - goblins, earth bears, and territorial gym monkeys - along with a level-49 Black Wolf that rules the dungeon. Jack begins a calculated campaign against the goblins, but their shaman responds by deploying stronger patrols. He kills a hobgoblin and takes its sword, then shifts toward hunting earth bears when goblin patrols become too dangerous. By chapter 9 he has learned that the Black Wolf is far beyond his present strength, so every smaller fight becomes preparation for the eventual confrontation.

Jack defeats the Goblin Shaman, despawning the goblin tribe and reaching level 15. He chooses the elite Pugilist class, which separates his physical attributes and grants Drill, a skill that penetrates hard defenses. The goblins' resource sharply improves his speed, allowing him to fight earth bears directly. He then battles the level-30 rock bear, the bear group's boss, until both collapse; the bear dies from accumulated internal damage and Jack reaches level 22. Jack delays despawning the remaining bears so the Black Wolf will still have prey. He heals in the Ice Pond and gains Pugilist Body. His next target is the ape group, whose resource appears suited to strength. The Black Wolf remains the required dungeon boss and continues to demonstrate power far beyond ordinary monsters.

Jack completes the Ice Pond's rewards and enters the ape territory peacefully. A boxing match with the group alpha ends when Jack wins but refuses a lethal finishing blow. The primates accept him, and he names their leader Harambe. Jack shares the dungeon's resources with his new allies and, through further waterfall meditation, develops a Dao root of the Fist. Together they attack the Black Wolf. Harambe and the primates suffer heavy losses before Jack kills it, only for its uninjured mate to appear. Jack faces the second wolf alone while wounded and exhausted. His combat skills advance under pressure, and he fuses his Dao into Calamitous Punch to create Meteor Punch, killing the second boss. The victory grants a faction permit, so Jack forms the Bare Fist Brotherhood and claims the forest as its territory, preventing the surviving primates from being erased by a dungeon reset.

After burying the primates killed in the boss battle, Jack leaves Harambe as guardian of the Forest of the Strong and accepts responsibility for Harambe's young son, Brock. Outside, he finds Volville controlled by Henry's Fang and learns that his foster mother, Professor Margaret Rust, has been kept under surveillance. Jack meets the djinn merchant Ar'Tazul and learns more about the economy of System resources. Edgar, a fire wizard whose parents were killed by Henry's Fang, joins Jack's challenge against the faction. Jack and Edgar assault the Volville Hotel, overcome its armed members, and confront leader Henry White. Henry reveals that he serves the Scion Gan Salin, but Jack kills him with Meteor Punch. Henry's Fang collapses, and Jack claims Volville for the Bare Fist Brotherhood. The town is free of its coercive ruler, but Henry's connection to Gan Salin creates a larger threat ahead of the integration tournament.

Jack recruits Volville residents, buys the Parkour skill, and appoints Margaret as the Brotherhood's Supervisor. Edgar acquires a Dao Fruit of Magic on credit and commits to Jack's faction. Margaret begins organizing Volville and explains that Earth's grace period will end under Animal Kingdom rule unless its people gain enough power and standing. Gan Salin arrives to claim Henry's former faction and tries to recruit Jack for the tournament. Jack refuses, defeats him in a rooftop battle, and takes his credit card, although Gan escapes through a teleportation item. Jack brings Margaret and Edgar to the forest, where they meet Harambe and use the dungeon resources. The Brotherhood decides to relocate its headquarters there for protection and growth. Edgar develops a Dao root of Magic. To keep the Scions from tracing tournament retaliation back to his faction, Jack drinks a disguise potion before teleporting away with Edgar and Brock.

Integration City rises as the tournament venue. Jack adopts the identity John Brown and registers with a false Dao and a flip-flop weapon, hiding both his faction and his Dao of the Fist. An unnamed cousin of Ar'Tazul guides Jack and Edgar through the city. Jack trains against an advanced robot and learns how wide the gap is between F-grade and E-grade power. Planetary overseer Galicia Lonahor opens the tournament under rules that eliminate competitors after two losses. Jack wins his first match while maintaining his false fighting persona, and Edgar also advances. Dorman Whistles displays extraordinary speed. Rufus Emberheart, the strongest Scion and tournament favorite, kills his opening opponent despite the surrender rules. Jack publicly accuses Rufus of breaking the rules and demands enforcement, leaving the ruling unresolved at the end of chapter 52.

After Jack challenges Rufus Emberheart, the judges assign Rufus a loss for killing an opponent who had surrendered. The confrontation makes Jack a public figure and a direct enemy of the Scions. His djinn manager begins turning that attention into sponsorships and tournament income. The Sage proves that his divination reaches Jack's hidden past, describes the Scions' covert arrival before the System changed Earth, and tells Jack that he needs a fund of two million credits for the coming Hand of God auction. Jack accepts the goal, buys a large experience ball on credit, and continues training against the advanced robot in his residence. He wins another match while preserving his John Brown disguise. Vivi Aragon meets Jack in person, and they develop mutual respect while watching the tournament. Li Shang demonstrates exceptional unarmed skill, and Jack learns that strong competitors may hide their titles. Jack resists Chen Zexi's soul influence and defeats her. Vivi then defeats Gan Salin in a fire-based contest, showing publicly that a human can overcome a Scion. She invites Jack, Edgar, and their manager into a Flame River alliance against Ice Peak and the Scions, and Jack accepts. Dorman Whistles subsequently asks Jack for a private spar.

The Sage demonstrates knowledge of Jack's concealed fight with Gan Salin and warns him to gather two million credits before the Hand of God auction. Jack uses loans, betting, sponsorships, and tournament winnings to reach that target. Vivi Aragon defeats Gan Salin and brings Jack, Edgar, and their manager into an alliance with Flame River against Ice Peak and the Scions. Dorman Whistles joins after a private spar with Jack ends without a clear victor. Jack develops a second Dao root, Indomitable Will, while Brock forms a Dao root of his own. In the last preliminary round, the sharkin Scion exposes John Brown as Jack Rust. Jack defeats him, but biased officiating assigns Jack a loss. Sixteen finalists remain. Three projected mentors select Jack, with an Exploding Sun cultivator winning the claim because Jack's Dao is linked to the faction's ancestor. Galicia tries to disqualify Jack, but mentor intervention reverses the decision and keeps him in the tournament.

Jack's Exploding Sun mentor begins training him in advanced Drill, Parkour, and the foundations of a personal fighting style. At the auction, the Sage buys a starship, Dorman obtains a Dao fruit, and the Scions acquire several powerful items. Rufus gives Alexander a Fire and Ice Lotus. Jack relies on loans from allies to outbid Rufus for a Rainbow Dao pill, a resource that may accelerate an E-grade breakthrough. Brock provokes Rufus, and Jack intercepts Rufus's retaliation, leading the Hand of God host to punish both fighters with fines and a temporary blacklist. Jack then learns that Exploding Sun cannot simply shelter the Brotherhood from the Animal Kingdom. His mentor offers to remove Jack alone, but Jack refuses to abandon his people. The tournament finals begin. Jack reaches level 49 and decisively defeats the sharkin Scion, while Edgar advances after the Sage resigns. Alexander, Vivi, Li Shang, Dorman, Rufus, and an eagle Scion also remain in contention.

Jack and Vivi begin a relationship while discussing whether their factions can resist the Scions. Jack then faces Edgar in the quarterfinal and wins only after enduring a complex multi-element magical attack. Dorman defeats the eagle Scion by combining Speed and Lightning Dao skills. Rufus overwhelms Li Shang and turns much of the audience against him. Alexander nearly kills Vivi in their match; she renders herself unconscious to end it, and Jack breaks the arena barrier to stop Alexander's follow-up strike. Vivi survives but loses her place in the tournament. With few realistic ways to evacuate or dissolve the Brotherhood, Jack sends his remaining funds home and focuses on advancement. He raises Drill and Parkour to tier 3 and begins trying to forge them, together with Fistfighting, into a personal Dao fighting style. The semifinal draw places Dorman against Rufus and Jack against Alexander.

Rufus defeats Dorman without attacking, using a Supremacy shield that weakens Dao he judges inferior. Jack then defeats Alexander cleanly and reaches the final. Exploding Sun offers a possible route to protect the Brotherhood if Jack wins and accepts discipleship under a senior elder. Training with Dorman and Li Shang fails to produce Jack's desired fighting style, but Meteor Punch advances and can now travel as a powerful projectile. When the final begins, Rufus is absent. The reason is an E-grade breakthrough intended to restore his damaged sense of supremacy. Galicia privately orders Jack to resign and applies concealed mental pressure when he refuses. The Sage advises him to wait, since Rufus is unlikely to finish before the forfeit deadline. Jack turns the overseer's pressure into a meditation challenge and begins an unplanned breakthrough of his own while allies gather around him in case the standoff becomes violent.

Jack's master realizes that he is entering E-grade without preparation. Edgar administers Jack's Dao Fruit of the Fist and Rainbow Dao pill, while Brock and Jack's allies form a defensive perimeter. Jack masters rather than submits to his Dao and forms an early perfect Dao Seed of the Fist, becoming Earth's first Dao-seed cultivator. He chooses the Fiend of the Iron Fist class, gaining a transformed body and Ghost Step. The triumph does not secure safety. Galicia bargains away outside interest in Jack, and Exploding Sun withdraws its promised protection under Animal Kingdom pressure. Jack responds by planning to leave Earth, seek rapid advancement and allies, and eventually defeat the overseer so his faction can claim the planet. Brock chooses to accompany him. Rufus fails to complete his own breakthrough before the deadline, so Jack is declared winner of the integration tournament.

Jack receives two Trial Planet tokens, an immortality serum, a soul-training item, and a D-grade robot bodyguard. He transfers his former training robot's personality into the new body and orders it to defend the Bare Fist Brotherhood. Galicia cancels his promised apprenticeship and authorizes the four Scions to attack. Jack's allies join the ensuing arena battle. Vivi and Flame River face Alexander and Ice Peak, while Dorman and Li Shang hold off other Scions. Sadaka is killed. Edgar defeats Gan Salin with an exhausting magical attack and collapses. Alexander severely wounds Vivi, then kills Li Shang as the martial artist protects Dorman. The healer Scion and eagle Scion escape, and another Scion is killed. Before Jack can reach the teleporter, Rufus returns from his breakthrough as an E-grade cultivator with a perfect Dao seed and demands the battle that the tournament deadline denied him.

Jack and Rufus fight as newly advanced E-grade rivals while the faction battle continues behind them. Rufus initially holds the advantage through superior speed, strength, and his king form. Jack retreats toward Integration City's teleporter but cannot escape. Under sustained pressure, he combines Fistfighting, Parkour, and Drill into Iron Fist Style, bringing their combat ability close to parity. As both fighters approach exhaustion, Rufus begins to fear death, weakening the Dao of Supremacy that depends on his unquestioned dominance. Jack seizes the opening and kills Rufus with repeated Meteor Punches despite Galicia's attempted intervention. Gan Salin then tries to murder the exhausted Jack. Brock arrives with his trained dog pack, drives Gan back, and carries Jack to the teleporter. Jack hides his titles, and Brock selects a random destination. They leave Earth for an unknown part of the galaxy. The Brotherhood remains behind under Margaret, Harambe's primates, its allies, and the D-grade robot, while Jack owes the Black Hole Church a favor for aid connected to his escape.

recaps.ending: After the numbered story closes with Jack sealed inside an ancient cultivation chamber, he survives a month of isolation, adds Weakness as a fourth Dao root, and escapes. He defeats Trial Planet's final guardian, then uses the Thousand Essence Flower to form the Dao of Jack Rust. An abnormal tribulation nearly destroys him, but he completes his D-grade breakthrough as a Cosmic Fist immortal, raising the Bare Fist Brotherhood to D-grade. Old Man Spirit helps Jack and Brock evade the Hand of God blockade and sends them toward Exploding Sun. Animal Kingdom hunters intercept them and reveal that Captain Dordok was killed. Jack kills the hunters and declares war on the Animal Kingdom. Gan Salin chooses loyalty to his friends and intends to return to Earth, while Nauja leaves her tribe to seek a wider life. On Earth, Alexander accepts Animal Kingdom support, becomes E-grade, and challenges Edgar to a death duel. Edgar accepts, leaving the duel, Earth's protection, the Exploding Sun commitment, and the larger war unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Hunted by the Animal Kingdom, Jack Rust and Brock escape into space, lose Captain Dordok to their pursuers, and reach Trial Planet with the uneasy help of Gan Salin. They befriend Nauja, uncover an ancient complex, and grow through the planet's successive rings while Earth sinks into war between the Brotherhood-Flame River alliance and Ice Peak. Jack defeats Bocor, survives alliances with Longsword and the three lords, claims the Dao Sprouting Pill, frees an Echidna Devil to escape, and seals himself in a cultivation chamber. After the numbered chapters, he escapes, conquers Trial Planet's final guardian, forms the Dao of Jack Rust, and survives an abnormal tribulation to become D-grade. Old Man Spirit sends Jack and Brock toward Exploding Sun. Jack then kills the Animal Kingdom hunters who report Dordok's death and openly declares war. Meanwhile, Alexander becomes E-grade with Animal Kingdom backing and challenges Edgar to an unresolved death duel on Earth.

recaps.text: Previously: Earth entered the Immortal System and Jack Rust rose as an unusual fist cultivator, gathering allies through the Bare Fist Brotherhood. He formed a close spiritual bond with Brock, the young son of Harambe, and came into conflict with the Animal Kingdom during the planetary tournament. Jack killed Rufus, grandson of Earth's Animal Kingdom overseer Galicia Lonahor, making himself the target of a powerful off-world faction. Professor Margaret Rust remained responsible for the Brotherhood's organization, while Vivi led Flame River and Alexander Petrovic led the rival Ice Peak faction. The tournament left Earth's alliances divided and its strongest factions competing for dungeons, recruits, and control. Jack and Brock disappeared from Earth's reach after the confrontation, with Jack still short of the strength needed to oppose the powers threatening his world. A route through the Balerian Outpost to Trial Planet offered him a dangerous chance to advance before Earth's grace period ended.

Galicia Lonahor answers Rufus's death by placing a galaxy-wide bounty on Jack, while Professor Margaret Rust fortifies the Brotherhood amid Earth's worsening division between Ice Peak and the Brotherhood-Flame River alliance. Jack awakens badly injured in Pearl Bay with Brock and realizes that returning home would expose both of them. With little money and Animal Kingdom hunters searching nearby worlds, they need passage toward the Balerian Outpost and Trial Planet. Jack uses the name Jared and secures work aboard Captain Dordok's Trampling Ram after proving his combat ability. The crew includes several seasoned fighters and a Sephira passenger who notices the weakness in Jack's assumed identity but does not expose him. As the ship leaves Pearl Bay, Gan Salin is being forced to help Animal Kingdom hounds follow Jack's trail. Jack and Brock are now moving toward their only known path to greater strength, but their pursuers have learned where they began their flight.

During the voyage, Jack studies the problem of fusing Dao roots and gains experience fighting in open space. A monster horde led by a D-grade creature attacks the Trampling Ram. Jack risks severe injury to save a crew member, earning the crew's trust and revealing that he is Jack Rust rather than Jared. Dordok and his people agree to shelter him within the limits of their strength. Animal Kingdom hounds intercept the ship near Amethyst Mountain, and Dordok fights them while Jack and Brock escape in a shuttle. Gan Salin joins the shuttle, claiming that he wants Jack's spare Trial Planet token and can help them flee. He stages Jack's recapture, gets the group through a planetary teleporter, and takes them into a Hand of God transit route. Behind them, Dordok is captured, one surrendering crew member is killed, and the surviving Trampling Ram crew escapes. Jack, Brock, and Gan Salin reach the route to Trial Planet, but Dordok's fate remains in enemy hands.

Jack, Brock, and Gan Salin register at Trial Planet, a world arranged as nested rings with greater danger and reward toward its center. Entry separates Gan Salin from the spiritually linked pair. In the Giant Ring, Jack and Brock find a vast forest dominated by oversized insects. Jack stays to train, allowing Brock to face real combat and begin proving himself as a warrior. Their hunts raise Jack's level, but stronger cultivators and giant predators show how far he still has to climb. While recovering from one escape, Jack accidentally forms the Dao Root of Power, complicating his future path. He and Brock disguise themselves with ant remains and infiltrate the colony that guards the route downward. They take a carved Staff of Stone, fight the broodmother, and become surrounded. Jack unlocks Brutalizing Aura, using fear to stop weaker enemies, then destroys the blocked passage and escapes with Brock. The pair descend toward the next ring with a new weapon for Brock and another major advance for Jack.

In the Barbarian Ring, Jack and Brock meet Nauja, a Tri-Lake hunter who distrusts off-world Delvers. She accepts their intentions and brings them to her tribe, where her father warns Jack not to trust the System and assigns the three a dangerous hunt. Jack and Nauja kill a level-121 Tyrannosaurus, satisfying the ring's advancement condition. During recovery, Jack absorbs his Dao Soul and discovers an inner training space containing a copy of himself. Sparring there helps him fuse Indomitable Will into his Dao seed and strengthen his body. Nauja also reveals that her people claim descent from the Ancients connected to the System's origin. Before the group can separate peacefully, Bocor arrives with an Animal Kingdom bounty party. Nauja pretends to abandon Jack, then kills one pursuer and helps him escape. Jack, Brock, and Nauja flee through fire into the Forbidden Cave, with Bocor and the surviving hunters close behind.

The fugitives survive a fall deep beneath the Forbidden Cave and discover an ancient sealed complex. Nauja identifies images of the Ancients, the Old Ones, Enos, and Axelor from her people's traditions. The facility recognizes her ancient blood and warns them not to scan its contents. Jack activates an Enos shrine and is drawn into five trials testing will, thought, body, combat, and acceptance of a divine gift. He survives overwhelming constructed enemies, is restored from catastrophic wounds, and endures the final gift's integration. The reward is a concealed life drop that grants a far stronger four-armed form. Jack tells Brock and Nauja despite being instructed to hide it. When ancient material is scanned, the System triggers an extermination response and alerts the Hand of God, which begins searching Trial Planet for remnants and plans to scan everyone leaving. Unable to return to her tribe through the sealed route, Nauja commits to continuing with Jack and Brock toward the Village Ring.

Crossing the Village Ring's desert, Jack uses the life drop to kill a peak E-grade predator and confirms the scale of his new power. At the oasis village, the group finds Gan Salin imprisoned by Bocor for abandoning the Animal Kingdom hunters. They free him, but the rescue becomes violent and brings Longsword's party after them. Longsword easily defeats Jack and offers faction protection that would save only a few people while condemning Nauja and Gan Salin. Jack instead wagers the group's freedom on a duel with Bocor. Despite the level gap and Bocor's armor and shield, Jack targets the exposed face, uses Brutalizing Aura for an opening, and wins. Longsword honors the agreement, releases the group, and offers Jack a place on his team. Jack refuses. The four companions enter the Space Ring ahead of their enemies, knowing Longsword's protection has ended and that the Garden Assault will eventually force the planet's strongest cultivators together.

The Space Ring consists of isolated biome bubbles floating in a dangerous void. Jack's group moves toward its dark interior to find an inheritance suited to Brock's Staff of Stone. Jack reveals the life drop while rescuing Gan Salin and fighting an elite electric eel, and the group reaches an ancient palace connected to the staff's Dao of Density. Brock completes its trial, gains a major physical enhancement, and secures the inheritance required for the next title. A D-grade monster then drives a vast horde through the darkness, but the Sage, Dorman Whistles, and Poppy find the group and guide them out. The Sage invites Jack to the Black Hole Church and claims it seeks to oppose the Immortal System and free Enos, though Jack has no way to verify the account. Jack declines immediate membership but agrees to investigate. Trusting the Sage's prediction of better opportunities ahead, Jack's party leaves Space Ring for the Labyrinth Ring.

The Labyrinth separates Jack from Brock despite their spiritual bond. Jack searches toward the guardian and accepts a temporary alliance with Longsword and Bocor for protection while looking for his friends. Nauja and Gan Salin remain together and find an archery trial, while Brock is isolated among monsters and short of supplies. On Earth, pressure from Vivi helps Edgar complete an E-grade breakthrough, making him the planet's first E-grade cultivator. He agrees to use his peaceful Dao of Magic offensively once against Ice Peak. In the Labyrinth, Longsword explains that advancement to D-grade requires forming a coherent Dao tree. Jack, Longsword, and Bocor enter a treasure trial together. Jack secretly replaces its prominent gray orb with a worthless pebble, and Longsword gives him the pebble without realizing the real prize is hidden. The uneasy trio reaches the Guardian's Gates, while Brock's crisis has pushed him toward defining an independent path built around strength and responsibility to others.

Nauja earns the foundation of Sun-Piercing Arrow and reunites with Brock, who has turned his new sense of Brohood into leadership of a large crab force. Brock, Nauja, and Gan Salin reach the Guardian's Gates and rejoin Jack. Representatives of Exploding Sun offer cooperation, while the Hand of God presence reminds Jack that its faction abandoned him after Earth's tournament. The gathered factions fight the Bone King, a D-grade guardian. The three lords bear the main burden, but Jack and the other cultivators join once it is wounded. Longsword delivers the killing blow, and Jack's group earns the Seventh Ring Conqueror title before entering Garden Ring. Jack finally inspects the orb he stole and learns it is a reusable peak-E-grade explosive treasure.

Jack joins the three lord-led teams entering Trial Garden. Lady Priya says Exploding Sun still wants him, but cannot promise protection for Earth without approval from higher authorities. Hand of God starships and deep-scanning equipment surround Trial Planet, increasing the danger that Jack's life drop will be discovered. The assault crosses lethal formations, with treasure hunters such as Jack forced to test routes for the stronger factions. The Sage, Dorman, and Poppy rejoin the expedition and expose a false treasure as an imprisoned Echidna Devil. The group refuses its offers and leaves it bound. After further traps and casualties, the expedition reaches the core, where seven formations protect the Dao Sprouting Pill. Elsewhere on Earth, Edgar's breakthrough enables the alliance to prepare a major action against Ice Peak.

At Trial Garden's core, Jack fuses the Dao Root of Power and trades his frost treasure to the Sage for condensed experience. When the last formation falls, Jack uses it to jump from level 100 to 124 and enters the lords' battle as their peer. He conceals his strength until an opening appears, defeats Lady Priya's golden companion, incapacitates Longsword with the explosive orb, and takes the Dao Sprouting Pill. Longsword and the Hand of God leader invoke faction rules to condemn him, while Lady Priya cannot claim him because Exploding Sun already has a lord in the contest. Jack breaks through the encirclement and flees. Pursued through the garden, he frees the Echidna Devil in exchange for immediate help and a promise not to harm him or those close to him. The devil kills or wounds several pursuers and departs, leaving Longsword and the Hand of God force to resume the chase.

Jack reaches the ancient cultivation cave while exhausted and still carrying the Dao Sprouting Pill. The Sage admits to his companions that he helped Jack obtain the pill because he values Jack's future friendship more than the treasure, but Jack's decision to free the Echidna Devil fell outside his predictions. The Sage, Dorman, and Poppy pursue the devil instead of joining the fight. At the cave entrance, Jack wounds more of the Hand of God leader's beasts and defeats Longsword for a second time, gaining a narrow advantage from his new title. He then uses the familiar ticklish pebble to disrupt Longsword's final attempt. With the remaining pursuers closing in, Jack pulls the cave lever and seals the entrance. The numbered story ends with Jack trapped inside the ancient chamber, holding the pill and committed to attempting a D-grade breakthrough because the sealed refuge offers no immediate way out.

recaps.ending: The Alliance defeats Ice Peak, Brock kills Alexander Petrovic, and Jack kills Galicia Lonahor on the Moon after reaching peak D-grade. Jonas Evergreen prevents the hostile fleets from interfering, then moves Earth and the Moon beyond system space. Jack survives, Vivi reveals that she is carrying his child, and Brock, Margaret Rust, Gan Salin, Nauja, Edgar, Dordok, and the recovering Sephira woman remain on the relocated world. Edgar cannot advance because his soul is cracked, but plans a wizard academy while Jack seeks a cure. Sparman remains critically damaged. The Animal Kingdom, Hand of God, former Hell warden, and Animal Kingdom ancestor remain threats. The Black Hole Church's disputed history, Jack's life drop and Dao-tree doorway, Brock's staff, and the approaching conflict involving immortals and old gods remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Jack Rust seeks enough power and political backing to save Earth from the Animal Kingdom. Exploding Sun conditionally supports him, but a political wager and Dordok's imprisonment lead Jack and his former mentor to infiltrate Hell. Jack frees Dordok, joins the Black Hole Church, survives a public duel sequence, and kills Maximus Lonihor before escaping home. On Earth, the Alliance fights Ice Peak while Brock, Gan Salin, Nauja, Edgar, and Vivi win separate battles. Brock reaches D-grade and kills Alexander Petrovic. Jack reaches peak D-grade, defeats Galicia Lonahor on the Moon, and secures Earth's immediate independence. Jonas Evergreen then moves Earth and the Moon outside system space. Jack survives as Earth's defender, learns Vivi is pregnant, and faces continuing threats from the Animal Kingdom, Hand of God, and a wider ancient conflict.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Rust emerged from Trial Planet as a newly D-grade immortal with an exceptional foundation, a powerful fist class, and a concealed life drop inherited during the trial. He leads the Bare Fist Brotherhood and is bound to Brock, his brorilla spiritual companion. Their actions made Jack an enemy of the Animal Kingdom, whose mid-C-grade overseer Galicia Lonahor threatens Earth-387 once its grace period expires. Earth is also divided internally. Margaret Rust directs the Brotherhood, Vivi Aragon and Flame River stand with it, and Alexander Petrovic leads the rival Ice Peak. Jack cannot safely return home without risking early intervention, so he and Brock travel toward Exploding Sun to seek protection strong enough to preserve the entire planet.

Jack and Brock cross Animal Kingdom territory under concealment while travelling toward Exploding Sun. On Darien, Jack discovers prisoners held by Animal Kingdom wardens and recognizes an Earth ally among them. He abandons his teleporter slot, attacks the camp, and defeats its D-grade leadership as well as a C-grade bounty hunter. Brock frees and organizes the prisoners. Jack releases the anti-kingdom revolutionaries, gives the Earth ally transport and funds, and learns that Earth remains split between the Brotherhood-Flame River alliance and Ice Peak. Returning home as an immortal could end the planet's grace period, so Jack continues seeking outside support. He and Brock finally reach Field Nebula, the Exploding Sun capital.

At Field Nebula, Jack reunites with his former mentor, now an Exploding Sun deacon, and meets Master Huali, a C-grade elder. Jack offers full allegiance if the faction will protect all of Earth-387 rather than only his own people. Huali tests the value of his rapid advancement and extraordinary foundation. Jack also reveals privately that he conquered Trial Planet's ninth ring, though he continues hiding the life drop and the tribulation connected to it. Huali accepts him as a personal disciple, admits Brock as an outer disciple, and promises to oversee an attempt to take Earth from Animal Kingdom control when the grace period ends. The commitment depends on Jack remaining alive and valuable and on the faction avoiding unacceptable danger. The Bare Fist Brotherhood consequently becomes subordinate to Exploding Sun. On Earth, Vivi reaches E-grade and seeks limits on the use of E-grade power in the coming factional conflict.

Jack trains at Huali's estate with a Dao magnet and regular spars, and he selects a spatial Dao vision for later study. He earns respect by drawing against a much more experienced disciple, while Brock moves to the outer planet to train beside Gan Salin and Nauja. Brock's strength increasingly responds to protecting and organizing companions. Huali's contest with a rival elder for the Grand Elder position makes Jack politically visible. A rival disciple provokes Jack into a public exchange of full-force blows, and Jack survives the first strike before killing his opponent with his return attack. The victory helps Huali but increases the risk of escalation. Jack then learns what happened to the Trampling Ram after it aided his escape: most of the crew got away, but Captain Dordok was captured and sent to the Animal Kingdom prison planet Hell. Jack accepts responsibility for the danger they faced and resolves to rescue Dordok and help the missing crew.

Jack deepens his understanding of space and improves his teleportation, but the succession conflict becomes more dangerous. The rival elder exposes Huali's promise to protect Earth and demands that Jack face a peak D-grade disciple. Jack negotiates a six-month delay and stakes both his place in Exploding Sun and the promised aid for Earth on surviving three strikes. With ordinary cultivation too slow, he proposes infiltrating Hell to fight Animal Kingdom disciples and free Dordok. Huali helps him study a supernova, while the library supplies a cultivation aid, an escape talisman, and a concealed early C-grade attack. Jack's former mentor agrees to accompany him. To shield Exploding Sun from responsibility, both men formally leave the faction before an Animal Kingdom contact smuggles them through the Eternal Gate in warded cargo. They arrive on Hell as unaffiliated infiltrators, with no settled escape route.

Jack begins hunting Animal Kingdom parties in Hell while his former mentor searches for Dordok. He kills large numbers of inner disciples and advances rapidly, but the prison world's warden recognizes that an infiltrator is operating across several zones. During meditation, Jack discovers that his concealed life drop has become linked to a life Dao root and the growth of his Dao tree. A door-like outline is forming in the tree's bark, and Jack's Dao soul can now act with limited independence. When the soul touches the life drop, uncontrolled life energy forces Jack into his four-armed form. Jack expels the excess power, but the resulting beacon reveals his location. Animal Kingdom cultivators converge, turning his hidden campaign into an immediate pursuit while the nature of the life drop and the door remain unexplained.

Jack defeats the force drawn by the beacon, including its Leonine leader, but three peak D-grade deacons pursue him. His escape talisman fails to hide him. Captured and tortured, Jack waits until all three are close before using the single early C-grade attack stored for him. The blast kills two deacons, leaves the third's fate uncertain, and nearly kills Jack. His former mentor rescues him, but Jack refuses to leave without Dordok. They find the Cyclops controlled by the warden's mark in a late D-grade hunting zone. Jack and his mentor defeat the controlling group, restore Dordok's awareness, and burn the mark from his soul. The rescue succeeds, but their planned departure is blocked when an unnamed level-249 Leonine Grade Defier arrives to confront the exhausted group.

Maximus controls the fight against Jack, Dordok, and Jack's former mentor until a mysterious Sage intervenes and extracts them to an underwater refuge. The Sage identifies himself with the Black Hole Church and reveals that Hand of God has compromised their intended escape. While the group hides from a B-grade search, he presents the Church's disputed account of ancient history. In that version, ancient humanity created sentient steel immortals as protectors, but the immortals turned on their creators, built the System to produce elite fighters, and rewrote the history of the war. The Church worships the imprisoned god of life and blames the god of entropy for manipulating the conflict. Jack sees an ancient vision linking Trial Planet, Brock's staff, and his former spiritual mentor to that lost war. He does not yet accept the Church's invitation, and the account remains a claim rather than established truth.

After three months in hiding, Jack has consolidated his rapidly gained power. When the B-grade searcher leaves Hell, the group resumes targeted raids using the Sage's divination and spatial extraction. Jack, Dordok, and the former Exploding Sun deacon destroy increasingly strong patrols while their recordings turn the Animal Kingdom's failure into a galaxy-wide scandal. The humiliation drives Hell's warden to request seven C-grade enforcers and brings scrutiny upon Galicia Lonahor because Jack came from Earth. The Sage commits the Black Hole Church to helping protect Earth. On that assurance, Jack joins the Church.

Jack's raids raise him to level 230, but Earth has only two weeks left. A rival Exploding Sun disciple provides Jack's former mentor's lifeblood to the Animal Kingdom, exposing the group's refuge. Hundreds of pursuers converge before the Sage's escape device can recharge. Jack's allies are defeated in separate fights, and Hell's warden stops Jack's final stand. With the group captured and no immediate rescue available, Jack uses the continuing public broadcast to demand a contest for everyone's freedom. The warden accepts under reputational pressure. Jack must first fight the warden's top disciple and then Maximus Lonihor.

Jack kills the warden's top disciple, then faces Maximus before a galaxy-wide audience. Maximus combines superior technique with a Leonine battle form, but Jack's foundation, titles, Dao roots, regeneration, and spatial skill let him overcome the level gap. Jack kills Maximus, reaches level 233, and publicly reveals his Ninth Ring Conqueror title. The warden honors the release agreement because breaking it on the broadcast would deepen the Animal Kingdom's humiliation. Jack, the Sage, Dordok, and Jack's former mentor escape in the Bromobile. Pursuers follow, but the Black Hole Church opens a costly long-range gate and escorts them through before a B-grade can catch them. The group reaches Earth's Solar System. The Animal Kingdom removes the warden and its ancestor takes charge of hunting Jack. Meanwhile, the Church arranges the secret return of Brock, Gan Salin, and Nauja for the war six days away.

Alexander Petrovic attacks Harambe in an E-grade dungeon, kills three brorillas, and leaves Brock's father gravely injured. Brock returns secretly but delays revenge to preserve the Alliance's plan. At the Grace Concert, the Brotherhood and Flame River launch their attack against Ice Peak before the planetary grace period expires. Margaret Rust coordinates the allied army while Vivi fights Alexander. Edgar and Gan Salin face powerful individual opponents, with Nauja initially held in reserve. A devil-bound Sephira woman isolates Edgar, and Alexander discovers that Vivi is pregnant with Jack's child. He uses her need to protect the baby to defeat her and prepares to kill her publicly. Brock intervenes, saves Vivi, and confronts Alexander on behalf of both Vivi and the injured brorillas. Jack has not yet appeared, and the wider ground battle remains precariously balanced.

Jack returns publicly and challenges Galicia Lonahor to fight him alone above Earth while the Alliance continues its war below. Gan Salin protects Nauja long enough for her to perfect her advancing arrow and defeat two enemy scions. Edgar abandons the devil's combat alteration, restores his original Dao, and frees the Sephira woman from the darkness controlling her. Their broken contracts destroy the devil, and the Sage revives the mortally wounded Edgar, though neither Edgar nor the woman can advance further. Offworld reinforcements expand the battle until the Bro Army and Dordok's crew arrive. Brock and Alexander both break through to D-grade. Brock's Bro Code lets him draw strength through his bonds, overcome Alexander's true ice, and execute him. Margaret traps the advancing Ice Peak army, and Ice Peak surrenders. The Alliance controls the ground battle, leaving Jack's confrontation with Galicia as the last unresolved major fight.

Jack clears a D-grade dungeon and reaches peak D-grade before confronting Galicia. His matured Dao tree opens onto an unknown expanse, but a vast turtle-like being immediately expels him, leaving the doorway unexplained. Jack also finds Sparman critically damaged after defending the Forest of the Strong and leaves the robot to conserve energy. In the broadcast duel, Jack exposes the life drop and declares Earth independent, causing the System to flag him for Hand of God containment. Galicia, revealed as Maximus's mother, repeatedly destroys Jack's body while his regeneration restores it. On the Moon, Jack converts his unfinished supernova insight into a stronger version of his signature fist technique and kills her. Jonas Evergreen prevents the Animal Kingdom and Hand of God fleets from intervening. Afterward, he moves Earth and the Moon outside system space. Brock, Margaret, Vivi, Gan Salin, Nauja, Edgar, Dordok, and the Sephira survivor remain alive. Vivi tells Jack she is carrying his child. Earth is hidden but not unreachable, and the wider conflict remains open.

recaps.ending: Jack passes Archon Green Dragon's trial by asserting a personal, fist-centered Dao, then refines and absorbs the realm heart. The inheritance raises him to five fruits, gives him control over the realm's exits, and leaves him with B-grade fighting power. He releases Brock and Min Ling, and the three head first toward Earth before planning further travel. Min Ling accepts that Jack is married and does not pursue her feelings. Jack deliberately leaves Spacewind and the rest of the expedition in Green Cultivator Town until he can safely deal with Spacewind, though he intends eventually to free those who did not attack his group. The Archon's realm can survive for millennia, and Jack is expected to return at A-grade to incorporate it into his inner world. The life-drop guardian remains asleep, Jack still owes the Supreme Blood a lethal repayment debt, and his promises to Dorman Whistles remain outstanding. Elsewhere, the Second Crusade seizes the Black Hole Church Cathedral after its guardian dies covering an evacuation. Boatman, the Sage, and other Church survivors are unaccounted for. A disgraced former Animal Kingdom warden orders a search for Earth, placing Vivi, Abel, Eric, and the relocated world in renewed danger.
recaps.in_short: After securing relocated Earth, Jack Rust leaves Vivi and their newborn twins to train at the Black Hole Church with Brock. He survives a hostile Cathedral culture, reaches C-grade, creates a trade in healing stones, wins a world anchor, and becomes Boatman's disciple. A joint expedition with the Hand of God enters a hidden realm that proves to be an Archon's creation. Baron Longform dies after ambushing Jack and Brock, while Min Ling saves them and joins their party. Trapped in the realm's deepest trial, Jack defines his personal fist-centered Dao, claims the realm heart, becomes the Archon's heir, and emerges with five fruits and B-grade combat power. He, Brock, and Min Ling leave for Earth, but Spacewind and most of the expedition remain confined. Meanwhile, the Second Crusade captures the Church's Cathedral, and a former Animal Kingdom warden begins searching for Earth to strike Jack's family.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Rust helped move Earth beyond System space and defended it from the Animal Kingdom, leaving the planet temporarily secure but isolated from the wider order. He carries an extraordinary life artifact, has ties to the Black Hole Church, and remains an outlaw in the System's view. Brock is his brorilla companion and closest cultivation ally, with a growing community of bros around him. Vivi is Jack's partner, while Margaret Rust, Edgar, Harambe, Gan Salin, and other allies help form Earth's new foundation. Former enemies have been defeated, captured, or driven away, yet the Animal Kingdom remains hostile and the planet's safety still depends heavily on Jack's strength. He has reached peak D-grade and must stabilize his cultivation before advancing. The Black Hole Church offers a route toward greater power, but following it will take him away from the people he has fought to protect.

Vivi gives birth to Jack's twins during Earth's first peaceful months after relocation. Jack nevertheless leaves with Brock and the Sage, travelling through many interspace layers to the Black Hole Church Cathedral inside a black hole. The Cathedral's crushing gravity and competitive hierarchy immediately expose how small their strength is on a universal scale. Jack becomes an outer disciple and is placed at rank 950 by the Head Envoy, gaining limited access to the Heavy Pagoda while provoking disciples who consider the placement undeserved. He defeats a C-grade will cultivator whose Truth Domain tries to exploit uncertainty in his convictions. The victory earns a Dao Stone but draws attention from her powerful husband. Dorman Whistles then arrives, heavily altered by a trapped treasure and unable to pursue his former speed-based path. Jack learns that low-ranked disciples cannot use the Cathedral teleporters, so returning to Vivi and the children now depends on both reaching C-grade and climbing above rank 800. The Heavy Pagoda may reduce the resources required for his breakthrough, and Jack promises to help Dorman if he succeeds.

Don Cranxiao, a three-fruit enforcer hired against Jack, repeatedly attacks Dorman and uses him as leverage. Jack accepts a lethal duel carrying a twenty-Dao-stone debt, then brings Dorman into his cabin with Brock. Attempts to develop conventional healing prove too slow, but Jack learns to compress life energy into healing stones. The guardian inside his artifact identifies it as the Supreme Blood, restricts his production, and hints at a stronger use. Jack discovers that he can fuse life energy permanently into his body, increasing his physical attributes outside ordinary System advancement. Two weeks of punishing tempering let him withstand the Cathedral's gravity without Dao and survive a higher Heavy Pagoda floor. When Cranxiao returns, Baron Longform appears as his cousin and protector. Jack chooses to fight immediately, overpowers Cranxiao's tyrannical domain and weapon with his enhanced body and four-armed form, and kills him under the duel terms. Longform pays the wager but openly declares Jack an enemy, while many low-ranked disciples begin treating Jack as their champion.

Jack's new body and life artifact carry him to rank 675 in the Ceaseless Murder Globe, unlocking unrestricted Cathedral teleporters and better training facilities. Rather than return home immediately, he spends twenty-two Dao Stones on his C-grade breakthrough. The process nearly tears apart his soul world and subjects him to a foundational trial of the Fist. After two external months of failure, he realizes he is not meant to reproduce an absolute ideal. He must affirm his own distinct fist path. That conviction forms his first Dao fruit and advances him to C-grade. Jack chooses the Gladiator Titan, King class and reunites with Brock and Dorman. Marcus William, a six-fruit swordsman and husband of Jack's earlier opponent, challenges him over their dispute. Jack refuses a delay, defeats Marcus despite the five-fruit gap, and wins a fifty-stone wager that Marcus partly pays through future wages. Brock remains at the Cathedral to earn status independently, while Jack finally teleports back to Earth. Elsewhere, three explorers discover a portal to an unknown hidden realm and plan to report it to competing major factions.

Jack reunites with Vivi, his infant children, and Margaret Rust, supplying Earth with healing and cultivation resources before returning to the Cathedral. During his absence, Brock manifests the Bro Code in the Ceaseless Murder Globe and earns recognition as an outer disciple. Jack uses the Fallen Genius Mirror, where visions of failed cultivators force him to acknowledge how often chance has shaped survival. He decides that danger does not change his chosen path. Further Globe victories raise him to rank 216 and stabilize his first Dao fruit. The Head Envoy then announces a joint Black Hole Church and Hand of God expedition to an upper-B-grade hidden realm, led by Spacewind, with Min Ling commanding the Church's C-grades if they separate. Jack is publicly offered a rare world anchor, valuable both to his current foundation and an eventual B-grade breakthrough, but only if he reaches the top 100 within a year. The announcement makes him a target for nearly every ambitious disciple. He rejects the chance to withdraw and accepts the deadline, while temporary rules forbid direct assaults during the competition.

Most of Jack's followers leave when the world-anchor contest puts them under pressure, but Brock, Dorman, and several others remain. Baron Longform finances a seven-fruit challenger and blocks Jack's preferred Dao Chamber bookings. Jack studies mortal lives to create Fist of Mortality, then makes a dangerous bargain with the Supreme Blood's guardian: he may produce one healing stone per day, but must repay twice the borrowed energy within two years or die. The Sage fronts the trade while Brock organizes distribution, providing enough Dao Stones to fund Jack's training and Brock's C-grade advance. Jack deepens his space comprehension, strengthens his body, and forms Space as his second fruit. At the scheduled duel, he expands the contest into a Cathedral-wide sequence carrying the world anchor as its stake. He defeats the original swordswoman, twenty-five registered challengers, and an additional veteran swordsman despite mounting exhaustion. The Head Envoy awards him the world anchor and six months of free Dao Chamber use. Jack absorbs it into his soul world, refining his Dao, improving his affinity with life, and preparing the foundation for an eventual inner world.

During the final six months before departure, Jack reaches rank 98, accumulates extensive resources, and forms a third fruit of life. He and Brock visit Earth, where Jack spends two weeks with Vivi, Abel, Eric, and his other allies before leaving without knowing when he can return. Thirty Church C-grades gather for the hidden-realm expedition under Spacewind, whose hostility toward Jack comes from jealousy over Min Ling. Boatman provides the starship. At the destination, the Church meets a Hand of God force and holds exhibition spars under a fragile agreement to cooperate. A venomous Hand prodigy deliberately maims Church opponents until Boatman orders Jack to intervene. Jack overwhelms her, prompting her A-grade master to attempt retaliation. Boatman blocks the attack and asks Jack to become his direct disciple, preventing a wider clash. In private, he makes clear that the choice is voluntary and that he will teach rather than rescue Jack from self-created danger. Jack accepts. Boatman gives him an inheritance seed and a cube of concentrated death energy to support a life-and-death foundation beneath his Fist Dao. The expedition then passes through the portal into the hidden realm.

The expedition arrives in a vast living jungle that appears to be an A-grade cultivator's inner world, with no portal remaining behind them. The B-grades head toward the core while C-grade teams spread out. Jack and Brock spare a tree dragon and share its ripe Dao fruits, then Jack begins learning the death technique Nihility from Boatman's cube. At a volcano, Brock discovers that the apparent treasure is a crystal-producing tree enslaved by a B-grade red dragon. He forms a voluntary alliance with its twig-like offspring. During the joint assault, Jack and Brock take six fruits while leaving the tree enough to survive, but Baron Longform traps them below the lava. Longform rejects compromise and attacks for revenge. The allied twigs intervene, yet Longform sacrifices lifespan and a Dao fruit for greater power, gravely injuring Brock. Jack creates Supernova from space, death, and stellar insight, leaving both himself and Longform incapacitated. When the others arrive, the Hand of God leader uses the missing treasure as a pretext to attack Church members. Min Ling breaks Jack and Brock out of a spatial cage and flees with them into deeper lava. Before escaping, Jack kills the critically weakened Longform.

Min Ling carries Jack and Brock through more than a hundred miles of lava and into the hidden realm's core temple. Jack recovers, shares the stolen fruits equally, and advances to four fruits, adding death to fist, space, and life. Min Ling reaches eight fruits, but the temple's guardians are dangerous even to B-grades. The trio catches up with the surviving B-grade expedition and is allowed into its formation on the condition that they neither fight nor retain discoveries. Spacewind and the Hand of God leader use weaker members as trap scouts and confiscate finds. A late B-grade black dragon then seals the group in battle. Spacewind forces several Church members to detonate their inner worlds against it. Jack protects Brock and Min Ling from the final shockwave with Supernova and regenerates only because the Supreme Blood's guardian intervenes, exhausting itself into slumber. After the dragon dies, the leaders imprison everyone until three patterned cubes can be solved. Jack recognizes their relationship to Boatman's Death Cube. After three months, he completes their life patterns, arranges a diversion, and opens the remaining cubes for his party. Jack, Brock, and Min Ling escape with a green bean and a wooden key while all nine surviving B-grades pursue them.

Spacewind and the Hand of God leader recover the first cube's treasure and identify Jack's party as the thieves. With ordinary exits blocked, Jack, Brock, and Min Ling flee through a forbidden shaft radiating A-grade pressure. They survive Spacewind's final attack and land in a sealed lava cavern dominated by an immense tree. A dead prisoner left evidence that a wooden key from above could activate it. Jack uses the key, and a message from Archon Green Dragon identifies the hidden realm as an inheritance site. Escape now requires Jack to decipher space-time runes and qualify to refine the Dragon Life Realm Heart. The activation severs the entire realm from the outside universe, trapping the other expedition members as well and defeating every attempted rescue. Over three years, Jack matures his fourth fruit, Brock reaches the same cultivation boundary, and Min Ling develops a ninth fruit. Jack finally resolves the spatial locks without force and enters the tree through a hidden corridor. At the realm's core, he chooses the inheritance attempt instead of an available departure. The numbered story ends with Jack transported alone before projections of the twelve old gods, while Brock and Min Ling wait outside and the sealed realm remains beyond outside help.
